quiz.q: What is the difference between a binary crate and a library crate?
options: A binary crate has a `main` function and runs; a library crate has no `main` and is used by other crates
A library crate can't have dependencies
quiz.explain: A binary crate produces a runnable program (has main). A library crate produces code for other crates to use (no main), like serde or axum.

quiz.q: What do all crates in a Cargo workspace share?
options: One Cargo.lock and one target/ build folder
quiz.explain: A workspace shares a single Cargo.lock (so everyone uses the same dependency versions) and one target/ directory (so dependencies compile once).

quiz.q: What should a pure workspace-root `Cargo.toml` contain?
options: A `[workspace]` section with a `members` list and (usually) no `[package]`
quiz.explain: The workspace root coordinates crates; it has `[workspace]` with members and no `[package]`. Each member has its own [package] Cargo.toml.

quiz.q: How do you depend on a local crate in the same workspace?
options: You can't — only crates.io crates work
Copy its source into your crate
quiz.explain: Cargo looks up crates.io by default, so a local crate needs an explicit path. You can then use its `pub` items.

flashcards.front: What is a crate, and what are the two kinds?
flashcards.back: A crate is one Rust compile unit. A binary crate has `main` and runs; a library crate has no main and is used by other crates.

flashcards.front: What is a workspace and what does it share?
flashcards.back: A workspace groups multiple crates under one root. They share one Cargo.lock (same dependency versions) and one target/ folder (compile once).

flashcards.front: What goes in a pure workspace-root Cargo.toml?
flashcards.back: A `[workspace]` section with a `members` list and (usually) no `[package]`. Each member crate has its own [package] Cargo.toml.

flashcards.front: How do you depend on another crate in the same workspace?
flashcards.back: Give it a path: `other = { path = "../other" }`. You can only use its `pub` items — the compiler enforces the boundary.
